nodes.label: PAM Module Layout
nodes.rationale: PAM is split into pam-* service directories (folder, account, account-template, account-rotation, session, web-access, session-recording, membership, project, access-request, discovery) with pam/ holding only shared enums, permission helpers, validators and the policy registry. Routes live under ee/routes/v1/pam-routers and DI wiring narrows new deps with Pick<>.

nodes.label: PAM Two-Tier Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Product membership (PamProductRole Admin/Member) plus resource membership scoped to a folder or account (PamResourceRole Admin/Connector/Auditor). Every list and mutation endpoint checks an action rather than mere membership, and there is deliberately no org-admin fallback: permission requires project-scoped membership. PAM endpoints accept JWT and identity tokens for CLI session launch and access requests, but web access and review/revoke stay JWT-only because identities are never approvers, and MFA-gated accounts reject machine actors since no machine can satisfy an OTP.

nodes.label: PAM Product Membership Reuses Project Roles
nodes.rationale: PamProductRole Admin/Member are stored as the generic admin/member project membership roles, so without a split a product member would inherit generic project Member abilities including identity CRUD, letting them attach an auth method to a product admin identity and log in with its PAM access. buildProjectPermissionRules dispatches by project type to pamProjectAdminPermissions/pamProjectMemberPermissions instead, giving members read-only visibility of members, groups and identities; anything not admin (including custom, which is how additional privileges arrive) resolves to the member set so a custom role cannot reintroduce project-level power. getProjectPermissionByRoles resolves project type too, so privilege-boundary comparisons measure against the PAM rule sets.

nodes.label: PAM Audit Log Scoping
nodes.rationale: PAM audit logs are served through the shared org audit-log endpoint but scoped by the PAM model in pam-audit-log-fns.ts rather than the generic project AuditLogs permission, so any new account- or folder-scoped event must put accountId/folderId in eventMetadata or it lands in the product-level bucket and is hidden from resource viewers.

nodes.label: PAM Actor Columns Come in Pairs
nodes.rationale: Sessions use userId/identityId, approval requests requesterId/machineIdentityId, grants granteeUserId/granteeMachineIdentityId, with exactly one set per row. actorRequestFilter and actorGrantFilter in pam-access-request-service.ts centralize the choice; hardcoding a column makes a machine identity silently read another actor's rows or none at all.

nodes.label: Consolidated Lazy PAM Project
nodes.rationale: Exactly one ProjectType.PAM project per org holds all folders, accounts, templates and memberships. New orgs get it eagerly and migrated orgs create it lazily on first PAM access; bootstrap seeds the org's current admins as project admins precisely because there is no org-admin fallback. The injectPamProjectId hook resolves it before any PAM handler runs.

nodes.label: Schema-Driven PAM Account Types
nodes.rationale: One ACCOUNT_TYPE_CONFIGS entry per type carries connection/credential schemas, icon, label and the sanitized-credential allowlist, and the frontend renders create/edit forms from GET /pam/accounts/types, so there are no per-type frontend components and adding a type is mostly a config entry plus an icon. Gateway extension points are extractGatewayTarget and buildSessionGatewayConnectionDetails in the same file.

nodes.label: PAM Connection Test (assertConnectionOk)
nodes.rationale: The test runs inside account create/update and throws to block the write when the target is unreachable. Gateway-routed types go through one RPC (testConnectionWithGateway to the gateway's /v1/test-connection) dispatched on mode: sql, mongodb, ldap, kubernetes, ssh or tcp, where tcp reachability is the ceiling for Windows RDP, SSH cert auth, MsSQL NTLM/Kerberos and K8s gateway-auth. CLOUD_CONNECTION_VALIDATORS covers host-less cloud accounts by minting credentials backend-side. A null result (gateway offline or missing the protocol) skips rather than blocks, so an old gateway cannot break account writes.

nodes.label: Cloud Credential Brokering Models (gateway-less vs gateway-injection)
nodes.rationale: Cloud types cannot use a plain gateway TCP proxy. Gateway-less (AwsIam, requiresGateway false) mints short-lived STS credentials in access() and returns them in session metadata; gateway-injection (GcpServiceAccount, AzureCli) proxies the cloud REST API through the gateway and injects a backend-minted short-lived token so no credential ever reaches the client.

nodes.label: PAM Policies vs Settings
nodes.rationale: Policies are governance controls (MFA, reason, session duration, command blocking) driven by the registry in pam-policies.ts and stored in the template's policies jsonb; server-enforced ones apply before the session starts and gateway-enforced ones flow to the gateway as policyRules. Settings (recording, password constraints, log masking) are a deliberately separate concept in the settings column, even though both are edited on the same template tab.

nodes.label: PAM Discovery (sources, staged accounts)
nodes.rationale: A source (credential account plus gateway) scans and stages discovered accounts for import; DISCOVERY_TYPE_CONFIGS providers return only { validateConnection, scan } and never touch the DB, so the service owns encryption, staging and fingerprint dedupe. Everything runs through the gateway (SSH-exec, port sweep, WinRM RPCs), which is why ssh2 is never used on the backend and scans produce no session rows, recordings or session audits.

nodes.label: Discovered Account Staleness (informational only)
nodes.rationale: After a completed scan, never-imported missing accounts are deleted and imported ones flagged stale (reappearing self-heals), touching only re-checked scopes so an unreachable host cannot mass-flag. Staleness is derived from the discovered row, not stored on the account, and is purely informational: it is deliberately not an accessibility issue and gates nothing (rotation, session launch, web access, import all behave normally). Do not add a staleness check to a code path; if the target is really gone, the operation's own failure is the signal.

nodes.label: PAM Credential Rotation
nodes.rationale: Scheduled and on-demand SQL password rotation (Postgres/MySQL/MSSQL) with config on the template and rotationAccountId (self or delegated) per account. Per-dialect SQL facts are reused from app-connection/shared/sql rather than duplicated, and rotation is brokered through the gateway.

nodes.label: PAM Session Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Sessions reference accounts via a nullable accountId so history survives account deletion, and orphaned sessions are hidden from all queries. Duration is capped at the template max and expiration is enforced by a delayed BullMQ job scheduled at session creation rather than a polling sweep.

nodes.label: PAM DAL and Search Conventions
nodes.rationale: DAL reads use db.replicaNode(), writes hit primary, all methods take optional tx. Search filters both tiers: ormify's $search (ILIKE) server-side plus client-side filtering on the immediate value for instant feedback.

nodes.label: PAM Deferred Cleanup (legacy tables/columns)
nodes.rationale: Old tables (pam_resources, pam_domains, pam_account_policies, pam_resource_rotation_rules, pam_resource_favorites, pam_project_recording_configs, pam_session_event_batches), pam_accounts and pam_sessions columns, and stale Redis queue entries are kept temporarily for rollback safety with removal targeted ~2026-08-01. pam_account_dependencies was repurposed rather than dropped, and rotation columns are kept because credential rotation reuses them, so the list is not uniformly dead code.
